title: A Letter Written to the Wrong Century
title_ja: 違う世紀に宛てた手紙
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の教材例。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: In a fictional literature lesson, students read a letter written by an imaginary character who addresses a reader living a hundred years in the future.
sentences.ja: 架空の文学授業で百年後の読者に語りかける架空の人物の手紙を読む。

sentences.en: The writer describes ordinary habits in considerable detail but mentions a serious public event in only a single sentence.
sentences.ja: 筆者は日常習慣をかなり詳細に説明するが重大な公的出来事には一文しか触れない。

sentences.en: Several students interpret this difference as evidence that the event was not especially important to the character.
sentences.ja: この違いは人物にとって出来事が特に重要でなかった証拠と解釈する生徒もいる。

sentences.en: Their teacher asks whether the amount of space devoted to a topic always reflects its significance to a writer.
sentences.ja: 話題に割く分量が常に筆者にとっての重要性を反映するか尋ねる。

sentences.en: The class considers why someone writing to an unknown future audience might explain activities that seem obvious to contemporary readers.
sentences.ja: 未知の将来読者に書く人が同時代の読者には明白な活動を説明する理由を考える。

sentences.en: The character might anticipate that common objects and routines would eventually become unfamiliar, while assuming that a major event would remain widely remembered.
sentences.ja: 日用品や日課はやがて未知になり重大な出来事は広く記憶されると想定したかもしれない。

sentences.en: Alternatively, the writer might avoid describing a difficult experience because it is emotionally painful or because its consequences remain uncertain.
sentences.ja: 別の可能性として感情的に苦しいか結果が不確かなので困難な経験を詳述しないのかもしれない。

sentences.en: The students recognize that several interpretations are plausible without any one of them being conclusively established by the letter itself.
sentences.ja: どれも手紙だけで決定的に確定しないが複数解釈が妥当だと認識する。

sentences.en: The teacher provides a second fictional text in which the same character writes to a close friend during the same period.
sentences.ja: 同じ時期に同一人物が親友に書く二番目の架空の文章を提供する。

sentences.en: This time, ordinary activities receive little explanation, but the public event is discussed at greater length.
sentences.ja: 今回は日常活動の説明が少ないが公的出来事はより長く論じられる。

sentences.en: The class examines how the relationship between writer and intended reader may influence the selection of details.
sentences.ja: 筆者と想定読者の関係が詳細の選定にどう影響するか調べる。

sentences.en: They avoid concluding that one letter is necessarily more truthful simply because it contains more information about a particular subject.
sentences.ja: 特定主題の情報が多いからといって一方が必ずより真実だと結論づけない。

sentences.en: For their own writing exercise, students prepare two short accounts of an ordinary experience for readers with different background knowledge.
sentences.ja: 作文活動で異なる背景知識を持つ読者向けに普通の経験の短い記述を二つ用意する。

sentences.en: They explain why certain details are included in one account but omitted from the other.
sentences.ja: 特定の詳細が一方に含まれ他方から省かれる理由を説明する。

sentences.en: Several students discover that adapting information for an audience requires reconsidering assumptions they had never previously noticed.
sentences.ja: 読者に合わせるには以前気づかなかった前提の再考が必要だと知る生徒もいる。

sentences.en: The exercise encourages them to examine the conditions under which a text communicates effectively rather than merely counting the facts that it contains.
sentences.ja: 単に含まれる事実を数えるのでなく文章が効果的に伝わる条件を検討するよう促す。

sentences.en: Literary interpretation involves attention to both what a text states and the circumstances in which those statements are addressed to particular readers.
sentences.ja: 文学解釈には本文の記述と特定読者に向けられる事情の両方への注意が必要だ。

sentences.en: An omission may have several possible explanations, and its meaning cannot always be determined from its physical absence alone.
sentences.ja: 省略には複数の理由があり、その意味は欠落自体から常に確定できるわけではない。

sentences.en: Considering an intended audience can help explain why a writer devotes attention to material that another reader might regard as unimportant.
sentences.ja: 想定読者を考えると別の読者には重要でないと思える内容に注目する理由を説明しやすくなる。

sentences.en: The two letters illustrate that reading carefully sometimes means examining the questions a writer believed had already been answered.
sentences.ja: 二通の手紙は丁寧に読むことが筆者が既に答えられたと思った問いの検討を意味する場合もあると示す。

vocabulary.definition: in a way settling a question

questions.prompt: Who is the letter addressed to?
options: A newspaper editor in the same town.
A reader a century in the future.

questions.prompt: What assumption does the teacher question?
options: Length of discussion directly reflects importance.

questions.prompt: Why might ordinary objects be described in detail?
options: The writer expects future readers may not know them.
The reader requested a shopping list.
questions.explanation_ja: 未来には未知になる可能性。

options: Only one explanation is grammatically possible.
The letter alone does not settle the motive.

questions.prompt: Why not call the longer account more truthful?
options: Different readers may require different details.
Truth is determined only by length.
A list of historical dates only.
Every reader has the same knowledge.
Importance is always measured by length.
Interpret texts by considering audience and possible reasons for selected details.
questions.explanation_ja: 読者と情報選定の理由。
